extracted.intended_audience: general readers and aviation professionals interested in the Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 accident and its investigation
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or evaluating a comprehensive Wikipedia-style article about an aviation accident, covering the accident summary, aircraft and crew details, timeline, emergency response, investigation reports (preliminary/interim/final), reactions, and references. The article should present factual data, investigative findings, and sourced commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flight recorder recovery and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: "Both the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) and the flight data recorder (FDR) were recovered from the crash site on 11 March." "The French Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety (BEA) announced that it would analyze the flight recorders from the flight."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A credible accident article/report should document recovery of CVR and FDR, where they were sent, and which agency analyzed them. Include dates of recovery and any major findings extracted from the recorders; cite the agencies (e.g., BEA) that conducted the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-agency investigation and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Ethiopian Civil Aviation Authority (ECAA)... investigated the accident. The aircraft manufacturer, Boeing, stated that it was prepared to work with the United States National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) and assist Ethiopian Airlines. The United States Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) also assisted in the investigation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document which national and international authorities and stakeholders participated in the investigation (investigating authority, manufacturer, NTSB, FAA, BEA, Interpol, etc.), the roles they played, and any offers or refusals of assistance. Good coverage notes cooperation, data sharing, and jurisdictional involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary report: timeline and factual data
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary report provided specifics such as timings, autopilot disengagement, stabilizer trim movements, thrust settings, and immediate FDR-derived measurements (e.g., "Approximately one minute into the flight... the autopilot disengaged. ... the stabilizer trim moved 4.2 degrees nose down...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An article should report the content of the preliminary report: a clear timeline of events, key instrument readings, control-surface movements, pilot actions, and immediate factual findings. Cite the preliminary report and quote relevant passages when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim report: sensor discrepancies and system activations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The interim report stated that the left and right angle of attack (AOA) values deviated by 59°. ... The nose-down trim was triggered by the MCAS four times. The MCAS design relied on a single AOA sensor inputs making it vulnerable to undesired activation and unreliable data."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters and investigators should highlight interim findings about sensor disagreements, automatic system activations (e.g., MCAS triggers), and any computed deviations. The article should explain how these technical findings might relate to the accident chain and training issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report must address human factors and operational issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTSB commented that "many operational and human performance issues present in this accident were not fully developed as part of the EAIB investigation" and urged thorough discussion of flight crew performance, crew resource management (CRM), task management, and human-machine interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete final investigation (and coverage thereof) should include analysis of human performance, CRM, task and cockpit management, and interactions with automated systems. Coverage should note where the final report does or does not develop these areas and include external comments (e.g., NTSB, BEA) about adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare with prior similar accidents to identify systemic issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The article repeatedly compares this crash to Lion Air Flight 610, noting similar MCAS-related issues and stating investigators found a "clear similarity" with the Lion Air crash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good investigative reporting and analysis place an accident in context by comparing it to prior incidents with similar failure modes. Document whether investigators explicitly compare data/findings with earlier accidents and what systemic vulnerabilities emerge from such comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding and regulatory response as safety criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Ethiopian Airlines crash, China and most other civil aviation authorities grounded the airliner over safety concerns. The FAA later grounded the aircraft as well, reversing a prior notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should record regulatory actions (groundings, directives, airworthiness orders), the rationale provided by authorities, and the scope/timing of groundings. This documents how regulators judged immediate safety risk and is a key outcome of investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification, mandated design changes, and training updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA ordered Boeing to implement design changes, effective by April, and stated that Boeing "plans to update training requirements and flight crew manuals in response to the design change" to the aircraft's MCAS; the U.S. Secretary of Transportation asked the Inspector General to audit the certification process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A thorough article should report any mandated design or certification changes, required updates to training and manuals, and oversight/audit actions directed at certification processes. Note which regulators issued orders and any stated deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design redundancy: avoid single-sensor reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim report stated: "The MCAS design relied on a single AOA sensor inputs making it vulnerable to undesired activation and unreliable data."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting technical causes, highlight design shortcomings such as single-sensor dependency and lack of failover. Explain the safety engineering implication (need for redundancy, validation, and fail-safe behavior) and any corrective measures proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot procedures, manuals, and training adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes that "the difference training from B737NG to B737 MAX was inadequate," that some procedures or manuals (e.g., resolution for jammed trim) were not part of Boeing's then-current 737 manual, and that pilots "did not complete the checklist fully" in some analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good coverage should evaluate whether applicable procedures and checklists were current, whether training covered the scenarios encountered, and whether manuals included necessary failure-resolution steps. Include statements from investigators, the airline, and the manufacturer about training adequacy.
